parsed.explanation: No trans-specific criminalisation, foreign documents face no documented friction, and the law includes anti-discrimination and hate-crime coverage plus a concrete custody-search accommodation for trans women. But exposures are real and visitor-relevant: police allegedly assaulted and sexually harassed LGBT people in a 2024 raid with no sanction, hate-crime enforcement is weak (one conviction since 2012), an LGBT centre closed after 20+ unsanctioned attacks, official hate speech is frequent, and rule-of-law weakness means recourse is unreliable. No universal-exposure measures (facility bans, registration, mandated disclosure) are documented, so the worst documented feature is state-tolerated targeting (tier 2) plus thin recourse rather than tier-1 exclusion. That places it near, but modestly below, the 0.65 reduced-risk anchors; imperfect protection without organised targeting or universal restrictions.
